metadata.title: Impact of PIRLS and TIMSS in low- and middle-income countries (questionnaire materials for World Bank officers and IEA secretariat requests)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a set of questionnaires and information requests about the policy and implementation impact of PIRLS 2001 (and related TIMSS 2003) in World Bank–supported low- and middle-income countries. It does not provide an analysis plan for student-level PIRLS/TIMSS microdata, nor does it describe sampling weights, replicate weights, or any complex survey estimation variables. As a result, there is no basis to specify which PIRLS/TIMSS weight variables (e.g., student design weights or BRR/jackknife replicate weights) would be used in an empirical scaling/achievement analysis. The materials focus on collecting respondents’ perceptions (e.g., whether national reports were prepared/read, media coverage, and perceived curriculum/policy changes), so weighting and plausible-value handling are not part of the reported methodology.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this document does not analyze PIRLS/TIMSS achievement outcomes using PV-based scoring; it is a questionnaire/information-collection instrument about perceived impact and implementation processes. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no statistical analysis of microdata (no imputation/deletion protocol is described). This is therefore a non-empirical instrument rather than an empirical predictive/causal study.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level analytic sample is defined. The document describes questionnaires/interviews collected from (i) National Report Coordinators (NRC), (ii) Senior Education Officials (SEO), and (iii) World Bank Officers (WBO) in a set of countries that received World Bank funding assistance to participate in PIRLS 2001 and/or TIMSS 2003. The appendices list which countries returned NRC/SEO/WBO questionnaires, but no inclusion/exclusion criteria, response completeness rules, or microdata filtering steps are provided.

data.outcome_summary: This document is not an empirical study of student achievement; it is a set of impact-evaluation questionnaires and supporting requests used by IEA in a World Bank–funded project examining the impact of PIRLS 2001 (and related TIMSS 2003) on education policy and practice in low- and middle-income countries. It explains that PIRLS 2001 and TIMSS 2003 were international achievement surveys, and it collects respondents’ perceptions about whether national reports were prepared and read, which findings were of interest to policy makers, and whether the project promoted public discussion or curriculum/assessment changes. The materials also request information about capacity building and the use of TIMSS procedures/manuals and released items. Because no student-level data, scaling model, plausible-value scoring, or statistical analysis results are presented, there are no performance metrics or achievement benchmarks to summarize.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse because the provided text is a questionnaire/instrument package rather than a research article reporting empirical analyses. There is no described ML pipeline, no target variable prediction/classification, no PV handling, and no missing-data protocol for microdata. Consequently, fields that would normally be populated for an empirical ILSA analysis (e.g., total_students, per-country student Ns, PV strategy, ML algorithms, and quantitative findings) are not applicable to the content shown.
